title: What did their last move threaten?
outcomes: Names what an opponent's last move threatens: a capture, a mate, or a fork
Tells a real threat from an attack that fails after the recapture
Says when the last move threatens nothing

steps.text:
After your opponent moves, ask first: **what does that move threaten?** Imagine they get a second move in a row. Could they win a piece, give mate, or fork? Look at what their piece now attacks and what it has just uncovered.
If the answer is 'nothing', you are free to follow your own plan.

steps.caption: Black to move. White has just played ...Re1. What is the threat?

line.say: Black ignores the threat and plays an unrelated move.
...Re8 is checkmate: the pawns shut the king in and nothing covers e8.

steps.text:
A threat is real only if carrying it out works. Ask:
**What would they take or attack?**
**After my recapture, do they gain?** A rook that takes a pawn-defended bishop loses material.
**Can they really play it?** A covered square or an escape square for my king can cancel it.
Sometimes the honest answer is: no threat.

steps.title: Same rook, one change
steps.prompt: Black's rook stands on e8 again. A white knight now stands on f3 instead of c3.
Before you looked, did you expect Black's last move to threaten something? Were you right?
